reason: Guest explicitly describes himself as an intraday/day trader who is in and out of positions quickly with no overnight holds or daily-bar rules stated.

universe.description: US equities, focus on volatile names and ETFs

setup.rule: Look for panic selling or short-sell restricted stocks after halts or gaps
setup.quote: You can buy reversals, you can go momentum. A lot of these stocks have become short-sell restricted.

entry.rule: Enter on reversal after extreme down move once selling exhausts
entry.quote: I'm a reversal trader, right? So I'm looking for things going down and then I'm buying them and they're turning around

stop.rule: Cut losses immediately on any sign of continuation; no stubborn holding
stop.quote: I just see red and I just start selling... Get out. Use a risk.

exits.rule: Take quick profits on 3-4 point moves; scale out winners fast
exits.quote: I need to take profits also because these things move 3-4 points so quickly.

sizing.rule: Increase size when profitable in the month; risk more on high-conviction setups
sizing.quote: once you have a bank roll... I don't mind risking more on good situations... normally what I would take 20,000 shares, I might take 70,000 shares

market_filter.rule: Be flexible; abandon preconceptions; only trade when seeing clear opportunity in volatility
market_filter.quote: you just have to be flexible. Once you see what you see, and if you like it, then go for it. Do not have these preconceived notions

ambiguities.issue: No specific numerical entry/exit criteria or indicators given
ambiguities.assumption: Purely discretionary intraday based on experience and order flow/panic observation
